markers.title: The check is the primary action, and its date sits on the page
markers.decision: The restaurant visits in this study looked at the physical setup as well as the software: the posters, the first-aid cabinet, the office. Those things drift, and a page about them is only as good as its last look. So the page states who checked it and when, names the next check as a day rather than a date range, and makes Mark as checked the primary button. The record of the check lives on the thing being checked.
markers.rejected: A separate compliance checklist in another module. It makes the check somebody else's job and leaves this page quietly out of date.
markers.pattern: Design system: page head with one primary action (p-page-head, p-btn-primary)

markers.title: A plan drawn in one colour, with numbers doing the work
markers.decision: The plan is flat outlines with rooms named in small caps and fittings as plain rectangles. Every item is a numbered circle and the number is the only link to the legend, so the drawing never has to carry a text label. That matters most in the kitchen, which holds the most items and has the least room.
markers.rejected: Labels printed on the plan itself. At this size they collide around the fryer line, which is the one place a reader cannot afford to lose.

markers.title: Every item says where it is in words, and when it was last checked
markers.decision: The legend repeats each location as a sentence, such as Kitchen, wall beside fryer 1, and carries the date it was last checked or restocked. The research found the platform was a configured product used through paper and people as much as through screens, so this card has to survive being printed and taped inside a cupboard door with no app near it.
markers.rejected: A location code keyed to the plan. Shorter, and nobody can act on it without the plan in front of them.
markers.pattern: Klook, numbered list beside a map — https://mobbin.com/screens/5ce8c0d9-c3cb-4724-a68d-50b770767ddc

markers.title: 000 first, and the sentence to say when it answers
markers.decision: The research found team members were never told where the reporting threshold sat, so each person set their own. The same principle applies here: nothing is left to be worked out in the moment. The call list is ordered by how serious the situation is rather than by role, and the first row carries the instruction to say the restaurant address first.
markers.rejected: A contacts table sorted by role. It reads as an org chart at the moment somebody needs an ambulance.
markers.pattern: Design system: list rows with a mono numeral (p-list, p-font-mono)

markers.title: The poisons line sits here, not only in the chemical register
markers.decision: A chemical splash is an emergency before it is a register entry. The number appears on this page with the reason beside it, and the chemical register repeats it inside each product panel. Repeating one number in both places costs nothing and removes a step at the worst possible time.
markers.rejected: A single canonical place for the number, with a link from everywhere else. Correct, and one tap too many.
markers.pattern: Design system: semantic icon chip with supporting line (p-badge, p-list-row)

markers.title: A gap in first-aid cover is stated, not left to be noticed
markers.finding: Team members described telling the manager first and doing whatever the manager said next. Beyond first aid, they see the rest as the manager's responsibility.
markers.decision: If the team's default is to follow the manager's lead, then the manager has to know when there is no first aider on the floor. The roster is read for gaps and the gap is written as a sentence with two ways to close it, rather than left for somebody to work out by comparing two shift times.
markers.rejected: Showing the roster and letting the reader compare the times. It is the same data and it hides the one fact that needs acting on.
markers.pattern: Design system: inline warning alert (p-alert p-alert-warning)

markers.title: Assembly steps in the order somebody does them
markers.decision: Four numbered steps in plain words, starting with the instruction people forget under pressure and ending with the one that keeps them outside. The visitor sheet step ties this page to the contractor sign-in, so the count at the assembly point includes whoever signed in that morning.
markers.rejected: An evacuation policy extract. It is longer, it is written for an auditor, and nobody reads it in the car park.
markers.pattern: Design system: numbered ordered list inside a card (p-card)
